title: Context-aware rollout SDK: shadow->canary transitions and idempotent control plane
creator: Ethan Brooks
description:
Goal: Deliver a developer-friendly SDK and control-plane API that make it easy to manage contextual rollouts (shadow -> canary -> graduated), enable safe automatic rollback on regression signals, and ensure idempotent operations / permission scoping for programmatic rollouts.

Scope:
- Control-plane endpoints to create/update/delete rollout policies and transaction-safe traffic adjustments.
- SDK client helpers (JS/Python/Go) to: create idempotent rollout transactions, apply sticky sampling, promote shadow traffic to canary slices, and observe rollout state.
- Permission model: role-scoped rollout tokens + audit trail hooks; minimization of blast radius for non-admin deployments.
- Safety: automatic rollback triggers tied to runtime metrics (latency/error), eval regressions (quality signals), and custom healthhooks.
- Telemetry: per-rollout events, sampling seed, exposed audit logs, and example dashboards for correlating model metrics to user-visible errors.

Non-goals: UI console changes (console work tracked separately), dedicated capacity autoscaling changes (handled by Dedicated infra team).
acceptance_criteria: Control-plane API endpoints for transactions exist and are documented (create, preview, commit, rollback, status).
SDK exposes idempotent transaction token flow and automatic retry semantics for transient errors.
Ability to convert an existing shadow config into a canary with a single atomic operation using the SDK.
Permission model allows scoped rollout tokens and logs every transaction to audit logs with requestor info.
Automated rollback triggers configurable per-rollout and able to be wired to both infra metrics and evaluation regressions.
Integration tests that simulate traffic shift from 0%->10%->50% and validate roll-forward/rollback behavior without user-visible duplicates.
Example notebook and SDK snippet that demonstrates safe promotion of shadow traffic and a graceful rollback on a synthetic regression signal.
comments: 2026-02-25 - Ethan Brooks: scoped the initial API surface. Chose transaction model (create/preview/commit/rollback) instead of purely declarative manifest to simplify migration path for existing customers.

2026-03-01 - Design review (Ava Chen): requested explicit client-side sticky sampling helper and seed auditability to ensure deterministic bucketing across SDKs. Action: add seed field to transaction response.
2026-03-03 - PM feedback (Diego Martinez): emphasize migration guide when converting shadow-only setups to canary to avoid duplicating model cost. Action: add 'shadow-cost-safety' checklist to docs.

2026-03-05 - Eng review (Luis Ortega): flagged potential race on commit with concurrent control-plane writes. Decision: implement optimistic concurrency with rollout-etag and server-side reconciliation.
technical_notes: API model: /v1/rollouts transactions flow: POST /v1/rollouts/transactions (body: basis: existing-config-id, changes: [{op, path, value}], client_token) -> returns transaction_id + etag + seed. Callers MAY call POST /v1/rollouts/transactions/preview to simulate traffic weights. To apply, POST /v1/rollouts/transactions/{id}/commit with etag. Rollback via POST /v1/rollouts/transactions/{id}/rollback or PATCH /v1/rollouts/{active_id}.

Idempotency: client_token used to dedupe repeated transaction create requests. Server must guarantee at-least-once commit semantics but no double-apply using etag and transaction state machine (pending -> committing -> committed -> archived).

Permissions: three roles - rollout.reader, rollout.operator, rollout.admin. rollout.operator tokens scoped to a project and can create/preview but not force-commit a rollback created by another operator (cross-operator promotion requires admin approval).

SDK helpers: startTransaction(client_token, basis), previewTransaction(transaction_id), commitTransaction(transaction_id, expected_etag), watchRollout(transaction_id, callback) with exponential backoff and transparent retry for transient 5xx. JS/Python parity required.
Sticky sampling: SDK will expose sampleUser(user_id, seed) -> bucket to ensure consistent assignment across SDK instances. Seed is recorded in transaction audit metadata for reproducibility.

Rollback triggers: standard set includes 5xx-rate delta, p95 latency regression, and eval-quality-score drop. Integration points: metrics pipeline (Prometheus -> Rollout Healthhook service) and external eval signals (Eval API webhook).
Testing: unit tests for idempotency logic, e2e rollout-simulator tests with synthetic workloads, chaos test to simulate partial network partitions during commit.
implementation_plan: Week 1: API proto & contract - finalize endpoints and open API specs; begin server-side transaction engine implementation.
Week 2: SDK implementations (JS/Python) for transaction lifecycle + sticky sampling helper; add unit tests for idempotency/retries.
Week 3: Integrate healthhook-based rollback wiring and create sample dashboards & alerts; build e2e simulator tests.
Week 4: Security review, run chaos tests, documentation + migration guide + sample notebook; cut rollout-2.5 RC.
risks_and_mitigations: Race conditions on concurrent commits - mitigate with etag optimistic concurrency and server reconciler loop.
Overexposure from mis-scoped tokens - mitigate by default scoping tokens to project and introducing safe-mode for operators where cross-project promotions require admin sign-off.
Customer confusion when promoting shadow to canary leading to duplicate cost - mitigate with a cost-safety checklist and preview that estimates expected incremental QPS and cost.
Telemetry volume for high-frequency rollouts - mitigate by batching audit events and sampling low-importance debug traces.
